content:
Warner Bros. has announced it is testing a brand new format with some iPhone users in the United States: HBO Max Shorts. As if vertical video itself wasn't annoying enough, the media giant says these clips are powered by AI tools...

The company says the AI is responsible for suggesting short-form content, with the final decision left to human editors.

"HBO Max Shorts" is designed to surface classic and memorable clips from the HBO Max library in a vertical, scrollable feed to help users discover things to watch. The feature's clips are powered by an internally developed AI tool that uses machine learning algorithms and scene-level metadata to sift through thousands of hours of video and suggest the most engaging and impactful scenes for discovery. Once the AI tool provides suggestions, HBO Max editors decide which clips best represent the stories viewers love, and these are then presented in a new vertical video format to ensure smooth playback.

Content is reportedly tailored based on users' viewing history; if a clip catches your eye, you can start watching it immediately, or add it straight to "My List" from the feed.

Warner Bros. says it is currently testing with a limited number of iPhone users in the United States, but appears to have already decided to roll it out to other devices and markets later.

9to5Mac's Take

Please, no. Breaking news to Warner Bros.: phones can also be held horizontally.
